Adaptive EQ engineering vs zh-Hans listing copy — two different jobs

Teams assume AirPods Pro capability in the binary covers storefront language. iOS, AirPods firmware, and Connect actually separate Adaptive EQ audio processing from product-page copy:

  • Adaptive EQ on AirPods Pro — inward-facing microphones continuously measure what reaches your ear and automatically adjust bass and mid frequencies to compensate for ear seal and fit. Controls how buyers hear tuned audio through supported AirPods. Does not generate Chinese listing text.
  • Ear-seal and fit compensation — firmware adjusts frequency response in real time as seal changes — no user-facing EQ sliders. Separate from the zh-Hans description paragraph that explains 自动音效调整 value to buyers.
  • In-app audio or EQ UI — manual sliders, preset pickers, or onboarding that reference headphone tuning. Your listing may mention Adaptive EQ; implementing custom EQ controls is engineering work, not listing copy.
  • Pricing and Availability → China — makes the app downloadable on the China App Store. Separate from language rows.
  • App Store tab → Chinese (Simplified) — independent row for title, subtitle, keywords, description, promotional text, screenshots, and caption lines. Empty or English here means China buyers see English fallback regardless of AirPods integration in the binary.

Working Adaptive EQ marketing in the binary and a localized China listing are both required when you sell on the China storefront — neither replaces the other.
